title: Mathematics on arXiv — weekly notable papers (24–30 October 2026)
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from claimed mathematical results, cross-listing, and sparse attention evidence. Citation totals are current totals, not gains during the window.

sections.title: On a Conjecture of Fiedorowicz
sections.abstract: The author proves that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of a finite monoid, using a mapping-cone construction and giving a 1,795-element example for the complex projective plane.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims every finite simply connected CW complex has the homotopy type of the classifying space of an aperiodic finite monoid; the paper realizes mapping cones to construct such monoids. The introduction states the aperiodicity strengthening.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The realized space is a finite, path-connected CW complex with trivial fundamental group; the constructed monoid is finite.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem does not cover arbitrary non-simply-connected finite complexes; the paper notes that a finite monoid classifying space has finite fundamental group.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The author states a resolution of Fiedorowicz’s conjecture, and the introduction says the construction uses aperiodic finite monoids; the paper spans algebraic topology, group theory, and rings/algebras.
sections.journal_ref: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: Primitive flag-transitive generalized quadrangles
sections.abstract: The authors resolve Kantor’s classification conjecture for finite thick generalized quadrangles when a flag-transitive automorphism group acts primitively on both points and lines, treating all almost simple groups of Lie type.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim that Kantor’s conjecture holds for all generalized quadrangles in this setting, resolving the cases where the acting almost simple group has Lie-type socle of any Lie rank.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The quadrangle is finite and thick; its flag-transitive group acts primitively on both the point set and line set.
sections.unique_caveat: This theorem covers the primitive point-and-line action case, not every flag-transitive action covered by the broadest formulation of Kantor’s conjecture.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: This is a claimed completion of the conjecture in the stated primitive-action case, bridging finite incidence geometry and group theory. The 97-page preprint states its scope explicitly.
sections.journal_ref: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: The Borisov--Nuer conjecture and root decompositions in even unimodular Lorentzian lattices
sections.abstract: The authors classify when every vector in the even unimodular Lorentzian lattices II_{8n+1,1} is a sum of two roots, settling the Borisov–Nuer conjecture and deriving an Ulrich-line-bundle consequence for unnodal Enriques surfaces.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that every vector of II_{8n+1,1} is a sum of two roots exactly for n=1 or n=2; they derive the stated Ulrich existence result for every very ample polarization on a complex unnodal Enriques surface.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The lattice is even, unimodular, and of signature (8n+1,1), with n≥1; the geometric consequence assumes a complex unnodal Enriques surface and a very ample polarization.
sections.unique_caveat: For n≥3 universal representability fails; finer criteria for negative-norm vectors distinguish sufficiently large norms and specific lattice conditions rather than asserting universal representation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors claim to settle a named lattice conjecture and connect the classification to algebraic geometry; the abstract describes a theta-series method for root counts.
sections.journal_ref: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: Extended weak order in all rank three Coxeter groups
sections.abstract: The authors prove that extended weak order is a lattice for every rank-three Coxeter group and deduce Dyer’s Conjecture A for these groups, using cleanliness of the associated Coxeter arrangements.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim extended weak order is a lattice for every rank-three Coxeter group and that cover relations are single-root toggles, as asserted by Dyer’s Conjecture A.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result concerns Coxeter groups of rank three and their Coxeter arrangements; the arrangement property used is that every biclosed set is hyperplane-separated from its complement.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is rank-specific; it does not establish the corresponding lattice and cover-relation statements in higher rank.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract claims a result for all rank-three Coxeter groups and a linked conjecture consequence; the paper spans combinatorics and group theory.
sections.journal_ref: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
sections.abstract: The authors prove an optimal-order upper bound for threefold additive energy on lattice circles and a uniform weak L6 bound for normalized square-torus eigenfunctions, with consequences for arithmetic random-wave nodal lengths.
sections.claimed_result: For P_n={z∈Z²: |z|²=n}, the authors prove J_3(P_n)≤C|P_n|³; they also prove a uniform weak L6 estimate and uniform Lp bounds for every 1≤p<6.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The arithmetic set is the integer lattice circle; the eigenfunctions are L²-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated endpoint is weak L6; the abstract does not claim a uniform strong L6 bound.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four mathematics categories connect PDE, combinatorics, number theory, and spectral theory; the authors claim an optimal additive-energy bound and Bourgain’s eigenfunction bounds for 1≤p<6.
sections.journal_ref: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: Minimal acceleration and the topology of premonotonic cocycles
sections.abstract: The authors answer Avila’s acceleration question for real-analytic SL(2,R) cocycles over every irrational circle rotation, relating the lower bound by topological degree to premonotonicity and proving path-connectedness of the nonzero-degree premonotonic locus.
sections.claimed_result: For every irrational frequency, the authors affirm the acceleration lower bound by the absolute topological degree and characterize equality at nonzero degree by premonotonicity; they also prove path-connectedness of the stated locus.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The objects are real-analytic SL(2,R) cocycles over irrational rotations; the additional characterization of uniform hyperbolicity is discussed in the positive Lyapunov exponent regime.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusions concern this one-frequency analytic cocycle setting; the additional characterization in the positive Lyapunov exponent regime is not a statement about all cocycles or spectral models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper states an affirmative answer to a named question without arithmetic restrictions and links dynamical and spectral theory; its path-connectedness result adds a concrete structural consequence.
sections.journal_ref: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: Local Law and Eigenvector Delocalization for Random Lifts
sections.abstract: For random lifts of a fixed finite graph, the authors prove high-probability Green-function estimates down to spectral scales away from singular energies, implying a logarithmic-scale sup-norm bound for eigenvectors in that region.
sections.claimed_result: For random N-lifts, the authors claim entrywise Green-function estimates at scales (log N)^C/N and, as a consequence, ||u||∞≤(log N)^C/√N with high probability for the specified eigenvectors.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The base is a fixed finite connected simple graph of minimum degree at least three; eigenvalues must remain a fixed positive distance from singular energies of the universal-cover spectrum.
sections.unique_caveat: Singular energies are excluded, and the stated base-graph hypothesis does not cover every finite graph.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four categories tie probability, combinatorics, spectral theory, and mathematical physics; the abstract gives a quantitative local law and concrete delocalization consequence.
sections.journal_ref: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities
sections.abstract: The authors prove a functional inequality stronger than Poincaré for uniformly log-concave measures, yielding sharp stability of quadratic-transport Brenier potentials and a Gaussian matrix-distance comparison.
sections.claimed_result: For uniformly log-concave measures, the authors establish a variance bound for differences of convex functions that gives a sharp stability estimate for Brenier potentials as the target varies; for Gaussians, they recover equivalence of the Bures–Wasserstein and square-root Frobenius distances.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The source measure is fixed and uniformly log-concave; transport is quadratic and the result concerns variation of the target.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated theorem relies on uniform log-concavity and concerns quadratic optimal transport; the abstract does not assert the same estimate for arbitrary source measures or costs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four mathematics categories and the stated link between functional inequalities, optimal transport, and probability provide corroborating scope signals.
sections.journal_ref: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: A logarithmic error term for subset sums of zero-sum-free sets
sections.abstract: The author proves a near-quadratic lower bound, with logarithmic error, on the number of distinct nonempty subset sums of a zero-sum-free set in any finite abelian group, obtaining the optimal leading coefficient and an Olson-constant consequence.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves f(k)≥k²/2−13k log(k+1)−116k, hence f(k)=k²/2+O(k log k), and derives Ol(G)≤√(2|G|)+O(log|G|) for every finite abelian group.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The set has k elements and is zero-sum-free; the lower bound ranges over all finite abelian groups, with no order or stabilizer restriction.
sections.unique_caveat: The asymptotic error remains O(k log k); this is not an exact formula for each group or k.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives a uniform quantitative improvement across finite abelian groups and links additive combinatorics with number theory.
sections.journal_ref: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: No Connectedness Lemma for Alexandrov spaces
sections.abstract: The authors construct Alexandrov-space counterexamples to both the ordinary and dual forms of Wilking’s Connectedness Lemma, answering a question posed in 2007.
sections.claimed_result: The authors exhibit counterexamples to the ordinary and dual Connectedness Lemma within the class of Alexandrov spaces.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The counterexamples lie in Alexandrov spaces; the paper follows prior extensions of the lemma from positively curved manifolds to orbifolds.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexamples delimit the Alexandrov-space setting and do not by themselves refute the lemma for positively curved smooth manifolds or orbifolds.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The six-page note claims counterexamples to both formulations and an answer to a long-standing question, linking metric and differential geometry.
